findings.summary: Q42 follows Q42: numbering skips or repeats.
findings.evidence: Q42. How do logging, tracing and correlation IDs help debug a production API?
findings.fix: Renumber so every question follows the one before.

findings.summary: Page 2 shows the 202-and-polling diagram and the timeout/retry/breaker guard table before the questions that teach them, which come on page 3.
findings.evidence: Page 2 has the diagram "POST /reports" → "202 + job URL" → "GET /jobs/42" with "200 / 303 result", the tip "Return `Retry-After` on the job URL", and the table "Guard | Timeout, Retry + jitter, Breaker". Q45 (202 Accepted and polling) and Q46 (timeouts, retries, breakers) only appear on page 3.
findings.fix: Remove the async diagram, guard table and Retry-After tip from page 2, or move them to page 3 beside Q45/Q46. In Q44 keep only a one-line pointer such as "queue the work (see Q45)". Also explain or drop the unexplained "303".
Run the fit pass — it adds material from the book without removing anything.

findings.summary: Q46 points the reader to a section that doesn't exist, and it uses "jitter" without defining it.
findings.evidence: "exponential backoff plus jitter (see Retry Backoff)". No page or topic is titled Retry Backoff in either part. The code `sleep(2**i + random())` is the only hint of what jitter is.
findings.fix: Remove the reference. Add a one-line definition: "backoff doubles the wait each try; jitter adds a random offset so clients don't retry in lockstep".

findings.summary: The cross-references to other pages give page numbers that don't match the syllabus order.
findings.evidence: "Token bucket and Redis counters are on page 8; keys vs OAuth on page 5." In part 1's topic order, Rate Limit Algorithms and Cache Patterns is topic 14, OAuth Flows is 8 and API Keys is 9, so neither number fits.
findings.fix: Use the real page numbers, or name the topics instead, e.g. "see Rate Limit Algorithms and Cache Patterns; API Keys, Basic and Bearer Auth".
Run the fit pass — it adds material from the book without removing anything.

findings.summary: The caption says part 2 covers Testing and Monitoring, but part 1 already has a page with that title.
findings.evidence: Caption: "Part 2 of 50 MOST ASKED API INTERVIEW QUESTIONS covers Testing and Monitoring, Scalability and Performance...". Part 1's last page is "Testing and Monitoring".
findings.fix: Remove "Testing and Monitoring" from the caption's topic list, or name the part 2 topic by its page title, e.g. "Logging, Tracing and Test Types".

findings.summary: Contract testing is listed as a test double, but it is a verification technique and not a double.
findings.evidence: ["Contract","checks both sides agree","two teams"] in the table headed "Double","What it does","Use when"
findings.fix: Remove the Contract row from the doubles table. Add Spy or Dummy in its place, or retitle the table "Doubles and contract tests".

findings.summary: Q42 uses "spans" and tracing terms before the sidebox defines them, and the page is labelled for test types and metrics whose questions are not on it.
findings.evidence: Q42: "Tracing adds spans: which hop was slow." The sidebox "Tracing vocabulary" (Trace, Span, Parent ID) comes after three tables. The metric table uses "p99 over SLO" without defining SLO.
findings.fix: Place the tracing vocabulary sidebox right after Q42 and the flow diagram. Define SLO in the metrics table, e.g. "p99 above target (SLO)".

findings.summary: The code comment says raising an exception opens the circuit breaker. A breaker is separate state that counts failures, and a plain raise does not open it.
findings.fix: Change the comment to "# give up after retries; failures feed the breaker's error count".

findings.summary: The example short code is 5 characters, but the bullets say a random code is 7 characters.
findings.evidence: "Generate the code from a counter in ==base62==, or a random 7-char string" versus "201 {\"code\": \"aZ3k9\"}"
findings.fix: Use a 7-character code in the example, for instance "aZ3k9Qx".

findings.summary: The polling/SSE/WebSocket transport table and the heartbeat tip appear on page 4, before Q50 asks the question on page 5.
findings.evidence: Page 4 has the table "Transport | Polling, SSE, WebSocket" and the tip "Send a heartbeat every 15-30 s so proxies and load balancers don't drop idle SSE or WebSocket connections". Q50 is on page 5.
